name: פעולה בינארית מוגדרת – מתי היא חילופית (באנגלית)
questiontext:
If \( {{CT:0}}\circ {{CT:1}} \) is defined to mean {{CT:2}},

what must {{CT:3}} equal for \( {{CT:0}}\circ {{CT:1}} = {{CT:1}}\circ {{CT:0}} \) to be true?

{{CT:3}} = [[input:ans1]]
[[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: Write out both compositions using the definition, set them equal, and solve for {{CT:3}}.
Step 1 — The two compositions
We know:

\[ {{CT:0}}\circ {{CT:1}} = {{CT:4}} \mbox{ and } {{CT:1}}\circ {{CT:0}} = {{CT:5}}. \]

So the question asks when are these are equal, that is when does:

\[ {{CT:4}}={{CT:5}}. \]

Step 2 — Solving for {{CT:3}}
Putting similar terms on the same side, and simplifying we get:[[if test="{{CT:8}}"]]

\[ \begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle {{CT:4}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:5}},\\ {{CT:6}}{{CT:0}}-{{CT:0}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:6}}{{CT:1}}-{{CT:1}},\\ {{CT:7}}{{CT:0}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:7}}{{CT:1}},\\ {{CT:0}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:1}}. \end{array} \]

(in the last line we divided both sides by \({{CT:7}}\)). [[else]]

\[ \begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle {{CT:4}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:5}},\\ {{CT:6}}{{CT:0}}-{{CT:0}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:6}}{{CT:1}}-{{CT:1}},\\ {{CT:0}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:1}}. \end{array} \]

[[/if]]So the two compositions are equal exactly when

\[ {{CT:0}} = {{CT:1}} \]

on_true.feedback: It seems you have formed your equation wrong. Remember that \(b \circ d\) is different from \(d \circ b\).
